root.name: Scandinavian Defense: Icelandic-Palme Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Nf6 3. c4 e6

overview: After 3.c4 Black offers a second pawn with 3...e6, aiming for quick development and open lines. Accepted with 4.dxe6 Bxe6 5.d4 or 5.Nf3, Black plays ...Bb4+, ...Nc6 and ...O-O with active pieces against an extra White pawn, while 4.Nf3 exd5 or 4.Nc3 exd5 let Black recover the pawn in a calm game. It is double-edged, popular as a surprise weapon.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn and consolidate with d4, Nc3 and Be2.
Decline with Nf3 or Nc3 and exploit Black's loosened structure.

black_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with ...Bxe6, ...Bb4+, ...Nc6 and ...O-O for the pawn.
Use open lines against White's undeveloped king side.

typical_structures.structure: Open game, White up a pawn, Black fully developed.

character.notes: Black gambits a pawn for development; White must consolidate under pressure, both sides take risks.

gambit.notes: After 4.dxe6 Bxe6 Black is a pawn down and White can keep it.

soundness.notes: Playable; not refuted, though White is probably better with accurate play.

structure.notes: Open lines for the pieces early.

approach.notes: Not a main line at the top; chosen mainly for surprise.

level.notes: Sharp but not deeply theoretical; Intermediate.

sublines_that_differ.name: Declined lines
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Nf6 3. c4 e6 4. Nf3 exd5 5. cxd5
sublines_that_differ.how: No gambit, quiet play with Black recovering the pawn.

character.reason: Black gambits a pawn for development; both sides take risks.

gambit.reason: Black gives a pawn that White can keep after 4.dxe6.

soundness.reason: Playable and not refuted, though White can claim an edge.

structure.reason: Open lines for pieces straight away.

approach.reason: A sideline gambit chosen mainly for surprise.
